# Day 25: Continental colour rendering sandbox integration + unused imports removed + redundant functions collapsed

Date: 2026-03-01
Goal: Integrate correct continental colour rendering from sandbox into museum demo master.

🔧 Technical Wins:
• Decomposed working sandbox code for correct continental colour rendering (rasters solved continent colour bleed) into existing 
  tectonics.py and ui.py modules.
• Removed unused imports like cfeatures, scipy.spatial, pykdtree, importlib, numpy.
• Removed redundancy; 
  - landmask_features and coastlines_features previously calling the same filepath, now collapsed into cob_features.
  - reconstructing continental polygons in rasterise_landmask() now calls reconstruct_polygons() instead of repeating logic.
  - reconstruct_coastlines now calls reconstruct_features using cob_features as argument.
• Continent colouring works!
• Added caching of reconstructed polygons so they do not need recalculating at each time step.
• Disentangled the time step from the slider widget in the UI into a function render_time(), so that a panel of interactive 
  dino icons can call it and reconstruct tectonic-fossil movement to that time. 
  Rendering logic was previously buried inside update_plot() inside create_ui(). 
  This is too entangled; I want multiple triggers, not exclusive tying of reconstruction time to the slider widget.
  Therefore the rendering function was modularised into its own function render_time:
	fig = plt.figure(...)
	ax = fig.add_subplot(...)
	ax.set_global()
	ax.set_title(...)
	plot_all(ax, time)
	plt.show()
  the function update_plot then simply calls: render_time(change['new'], out), making the slider just a trigger for the 
  underlying rendering function.
  This explicit separation now allows something like e.g. render_time(145) for one dino asset, render_time(68) for another dino...

🪛 Next (for museum demo purposes):
• Add a simple dictionary: DINO_TIMES = {
				"trex":68,
				"triceratops":70,
				"velociraptor":75
}
• Build a Panel grid
• Connect each image to render_time
